items.summary: The bulk of the fresh funding financed the cash-and-stock deal as the catering startup targets ₹700 crore in revenue this fiscal year through market consolidation.

items.summary: The Samarth 2.0, announced in the budget for 2026–27, aims to modernise the existing skilling framework through closer collaboration between industry and academic institutions, with a focus on preparing workers for the changing technology and industry requirements.

items.title: India a keystone for Hitachi Energy supply chain amid global power crunch: CEO
items.summary: Hitachi Energy CEO Andreas Schierenbeck said rising demand from data centres and the shift from oil and gas to electricity across industries have intensified industrial power needs in recent years, creating a mismatch between supply and demand.

items.title: Public sector banks' Rs 7.8 lakh crore corporate loan pipeline signals capex revival
items.summary: Public sector banks have revealed a corporate loan pipeline of approximately ₹7.8 lakh crore signaling increased credit demand. Companies are stepping up their investment, particularly in sectors like renewable energy and semiconductor manufacturing. Banks report varied corporate credit growth, with some institutions witnessing over 50% increase year-on-year. Mid-sized and large companies are leading the way in capital expenditure, while smaller suppliers are also finding opportunities.

items.title: KKR to invest over ₹6,000 crore in Petronas India RE arm
items.summary: KKR plans to invest more than ₹6,000 crore in Gentari Renewable India, which is Petronas' renewable energy unit. The funding aims to support the expansion of its renewable energy and green hydrogen projects. Gentari has previously acquired a 1.6 gigawatt renewable energy portfolio and is seeking financial partners. This investment will also facilitate the acquisition of stakes in existing joint ventures in India.

items.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
items.summary: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.

items.title: Sydney’s New $4 Billion Airport Opens With Barely Any Flights
items.summary: After more than half a century of political procrastination, environmental protests and funding shortfalls, Sydney finally has a second airport. But the new A$5.6 billion ($4 billion) site’s commercial prospects are already in question.

items.title: Challenges ahead for Fairfax's management of IDBI Bank post ₹52,878 crore stake deal approval
items.summary: Fairfax Financial's subsidiary has acquired a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, leading to potential operational changes. The new management faces challenges such as employee resistance and asset quality improvement. Despite having a higher profitability compared to peers, IDBI Bank's gross non-performing asset ratio remains concerning. The bank's success will rely on its ability to enhance asset quality while maintaining earnings growth.

items.title: Correcting rupee against fundamentals ultimately futile, says RBI's ex-guv Subbarao
items.summary: D Subbarao advocates for allowing the rupee to find its level based on economic fundamentals. He criticizes costly short-term measures that do not address structural issues behind capital outflows. The rupee's recent recovery followed the Reserve Bank of India's measures to reduce dollar demand. Subbarao highlights the importance of tax reforms to attract foreign investment in India.

items.title: Reality shows, cricket turn advertisers' safe bets
items.summary: Established non-fiction shows such as Bigg Boss and Kaun Banega Crorepati have continued to attract advertisers despite the blackout. Bigg Boss has roped in 95 sponsors across its language editions, while KBC has secured 25 sponsors. Cricket is also drawing advertiser interest, with India matches providing an opportunity to reach large audiences in a second half of the year largely devoid of marquee events such as the IPL or ICC tournaments. The India-West Indies series has drawn a strong response from brands, while the India-New Zealand series is also expected to see strong traction.

items.title: PM-KUSUM 2.0 may be aligned with farm schemes: Renewable energy secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi
items.summary: The government plans to expand PM KUSUM to include incentives for modern irrigation practices among farmers. This expansion will encourage the use of solar-powered water pumps and promote remunerative crops. The ministries of renewable energy and agriculture are collaborating to align this initiative with existing schemes. New components such as agrivoltaics will also be integrated in the next phase.

items.title: Private banks' margins fall as FCNR deposits raise funding costs
items.summary: In the second quarter, leading private sector banks in India reported a drop in net interest margins. This decline was primarily caused by the costs associated with foreign currency non-resident deposits. Analysts noted that the leveraged nature of these deposits significantly impacted profitability. Additionally, banks faced pressure from faster repricing of assets as interest rates declined.

items.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
items.summary: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

items.title: Farmers face 15% loss as poultry feed costs surge
items.summary: Poultry farmers are currently experiencing losses of approximately 15% due to rising livestock feed costs. Key ingredients have seen price increases of up to 75%, affecting farmers' ability to cope. Dairy producers, particularly in drought-affected regions, struggle to source necessary fodder for their livestock. Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

items.title: Who is Amal Kelshikar? Why did he resign from the position of Torrent Pharmaceuticals' Executive Director? Explained
items.summary: Torrent Pharmaceuticals accepted Executive Director Amal Kelshikar’s resignation, effective at the close of business on 16 October 2026. Kelshikar said in his resignation letter that he was stepping down after reflection and believed it was the right time to transition.

items.title: Meta revises terms governing website content: What's new and changed? What rights do publishers retain now? Explained
items.summary: Meta will update its website terms on 30 October, removing explicit language authorising the use of crawled content to train its products. The terms still allow automated crawling and collection, with stated purposes narrowed to advertising and business products and product security.

items.title: India vs China in 40 years: TRUST MF CIO Mihir Vora - 'India compounded GDP growth at 7.3%; China broke out at 11.3%'
items.summary: TRUST Mutual Fund CIO Mihir Vora said India's GDP expanded 15.7-fold in 40 years, compared with China's 65.1-fold growth. He attributed the divergence to a gap in annualised growth rates and urged India to address obstacles to ease of doing business.

items.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
items.summary: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.

items.title: India's exports rise across geographies; Africa, ASEAN lead growth in Apr-Aug
items.summary: India's merchandise exports increased significantly across different regions from April to August this fiscal year. Exports to Africa saw a notable rise of 47 percent, reaching USD 26.19 billion. The ASEAN region also experienced a substantial growth of 56 percent in exports, totaling USD 23.08 billion. Furthermore, shipments to North-East Asia rose by 37 percent, amounting to USD 21.03 billion. Overall, India's total merchandise exports rose by 18.

items.title: The bloated workweek is coming for Sundays—as some embrace flexibility, others worry about job security
items.summary: A new report finds nearly half of workers are often logging in on Sundays. It is a boon for worker flexibility, or a sign of job-hugging insecurity?

items.title: Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report
items.summary: India's services trade surplus has declined as imports grew faster than exports, leading to concerns about foreign exchange earnings. In September 2026, net services exports fell by 10 percent to USD 16.9 billion. Despite strong growth in merchandise exports of 23 percent, the services sector faces challenges. While cumulative net services exports increased during the first half, their sustainability is uncertain.

items.summary: India needs to maintain policy credibility and continuity to sustain foreign investment inflows, as strong economic growth alone may not be enough to reassure global investors about the country's long-term business environment, highlighted Kyunghoon Kim, Head of the India and South Asia Team at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP).

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week to strengthen bilateral relations and discuss trade issues. items.summary: India's soybean production forecast indicates a slight decline to 107.93 lakh tonnes during the ongoing Kharif season. Drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana are contributing to this reduction in output. However, increased production in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan is expected to compensate for these losses. The area cultivated with soybean increased by approximately 5 lakh hectares compared to the previous season.

items.title: 'India an important ally': Rubio says Trump weighing impact of Russia-related tariffs
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that India's energy requirements will be considered before possible sanctions on Russian oil. President Donald Trump recently waived certain provisions of a proposed sanctions law affecting major importers of Russian crude. Rubio emphasized the need for time to assess the impact of these measures on global economies. He highlighted the strategic partnership with India as an important factor in decision-making.

items.title: Christmas cheer, but caution remains: Exporters welcome US tariff relief, keep diversification plans
items.summary: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive proposed tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil has eased uncertainty for Indian exporters ahead of the crucial Christmas shipping season. However, businesses across textiles, gems and jewellery, and human hair products say they will continue diversifying export markets after last year’s tariff turmoil, even as the US remains a key destination for Indian goods.

items.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
items.summary: India will implement duty concessions for certain imports from New Zealand starting October 20, under a new FTA. The concessions include zero basic customs duty for sheep meat and specific rates for fish and wine. Additionally, provisions have been made for manuka honey and kiwi fruit imports with varying duties. Sensitive categories like dairy products are excluded from this trade liberalization agreement.
